newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 8.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Floods in the east and northeast of the Czech Republic have now taken seven lives and wounded other people. According to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus 21 helicopters and 60 military vehicles have been sent to the areas. Interior Minister Jan Ruml, Environment Minister Jiri Skalicky, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux and Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny left for the areas yesterday.
- Environmental activists called off their blockade of the Temelin Nuclear Power Plant yesterday due to the rain. The blockade will probably continue on Tuesday.
- Agrobanka obtained another loan from the Housing Guarantee Program to aid housing in the Czech Republic. The minimum amount for 15 years is three million crowns.
- Ceska Pojistovna immediately reacted to the situations caused by the floods and began providing initial deposits to its customers for damages caused already yesterday.
- The Austrian paper company Duropack Vienna AG increased its stake in Bupak Obaly Ceske Budejovice to 60 percent from 51 percent.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Vaclav Klaus addressed parliament yesterday, evaluating the activities of the cabinet for the past year. He said the cabinet has a clear vision for the future, the vision of a stable, respectable and standard European country. Parliament Chairman and Social Democratic leader Milos Zeman said this vision is a heterogeneous dream, which does not offer certainty.

- Due to the floods, several companies in the east were forced to close shop and send their workers home. These include Perla, Bravo, Karado, Primona, Lineta, Barum Continental and Prumysl Mlecne Vyroby.
- The investment company O.B. Invest, which was placed under forced administration last week, and its mother company CSOB bank are preparing to fix the problems in Kvanto funds.

- Skoda Plzen is no longer interested in buying a 54-percent stake in Skoda Praha from the state. Cimex, however, is still interested in Skoda Praha, which is the main supplier for the Temelin Nuclear Power Plant.
- According to Czechtrade, the Ukrainian company Lilija wants to buy one million litres of Czech spirits each month.

- Goliard, which obtained more than one third of Olma Olomouc last month from Austrian Credit Investment Bank has not yet announced who it will sell the stake to. Most probably, it will go on order to a western European food concern. Danone, for instance, has shown interest.
- Skoda plans to invest several billion crowns into production of Octavia automobiles in order to meet domestic demand. During next year, it should be able to make up to one third more units.
PRAVO - The State Veterinary Administration banned imports of live pigs, including black pigs, from Belgium to the Czech Republic, effective immediately, due to swine fever in Belgium.
- CEZ would like to build a new energy source with power of around 1,100 megawatts by the year 2005 with a mining company and possibly another partner.
- From July 8, Konsolidacni Banka is decreasing its base rate I by 1.25 percentage points to 16.75 percent and its interest rate for newly issued credits by 1.25 percent to 17.75 percent.
- Unemployment in June 1997 was four percent, an increase of 0.2 percent over May, when it was 3.8 percent.

- According to a spokesman for Czech Railways, Daniel Bacik, Czech Railways owes money to all its energy suppliers, for instance 80 million crowns to Severomoravska Energetika, 30 million to Jihomoravska Energetika and 40 million to Vychodoceska Energetika.
- A decision will be made today over how much practitioners will receive for their work from insurance companies. On Monday, doctors began returning money to patients.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Estimates for the June increase in the inflation rate over May are between about 0.4 and 1.6 percent.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Parliament Chairman Milos Zeman will fly to northern Moravia today to visit areas affected by the flood.
- The Foreign Ministry sent a special aircraft to help Czech tourists stranded on holidays in Greece due to the insolvency of travel agencies Oasis Tours and Travela.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
